key_insight: GLASS improves scalable all-atom crystal generation by moving correspondence handling out of the generative flow: it learns a permutation-invariant global latent and uses slot-based parallel decoding to build atoms without atom-wise transport.
engineering_relevance: This makes generation of larger crystals and MOFs more practical, especially when atom counts grow and particle-space methods struggle with reliability and training cost.
method: Encode each structure into a permutation-invariant global latent space.
Train the latent distribution with flow matching.
Decode atoms in parallel with learned slots, avoiding index-based correspondence during generation.
evidence_signal: On MP20, GLASS matches particle-space baselines and reaches the validity of the training data across structure sizes; on a QMOF subset, it generates MOFs with up to 150 atoms per unit cell and approaches training-data validity.
watch_item: Novelty is constrained by a validity–novelty tradeoff, and MOF novelty is further limited by the autoencoder’s generalization on the available data.
paper_title: GLASS: Global Latent Aggregation with Slot-based Set Decoding for Scalable All-Atom Crystal Generation
